title: Gucci Guilty vs Armani Code
summary: Gucci Guilty Pour Femme vs Armani Code: a layered amber floral against a soft tonka oriental. Compare notes, longevity, and which suits you on Scentbird.
body_markdown:
Some fragrance comparisons come down to which notes are used. The Gucci Guilty Pour Femme vs Armani Code one comes down to pace. Both eventually settle into a warm, ambery base, but[Gucci Guilty Pour Femme](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/gucci-guilty-pour-femme-1429) gets there by way of three distinct stages, while Armani Code barely changes shape at all between the first spray and the last hour.


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme, available on Scentbird.


## Gucci Guilty Pour Femme vs Armani Code: what they share


Both fragrances land on a warm, faintly sweet base, amber and vanilla in one case, tonka bean in the other, and both were built with going-out occasions in mind rather than daytime errands. Neither one opens with much citrus brightness that lasts, and both are frequently the fragrance someone reaches for specifically because it reads as a little more grown-up than a fresh, everyday scent. Both also came from the same general design era of the 2000s and 2010s, when a warm amber base was treated as the standard finish for a going-out fragrance rather than an unusual choice. From there, the two compositions part ways almost entirely.


## Gucci Guilty Pour Femme


What lingers on a scarf or a coat sleeve long after Gucci Guilty Pour Femme has faded from skin is the base, not the opening: amber, patchouli, and white musk, warmed by a trace of vanilla, the part of the composition built to outlast the peach and lilac stacked above it. Aurelien Guichard composed the fragrance for Gucci in 2010, opening on pink pepper and peach before geranium takes the heart, and total wear typically runs seven to nine hours with the strongest sillage in the earlier hours. The catch is that the fruity-floral opening people are often drawn to is genuinely brief, fading within roughly the first hour, so shopping for that specific combination means chasing an impression that doesn’t stay. Skip it if the peach-lilac opening is the exact reason you want the bottle.


## Armani Code


Antoine Lie composed Armani Code for Giorgio Armani in 2004 around lemon and bergamot, a top that fades quickly into olive blossom before the fragrance settles into tonka bean, leather, and soft woods for the remainder of the wear. Unlike many fragrances built around a warm base, Code doesn’t so much evolve as arrive early and stay there, smooth and softly sweet with almost no sharp turns. Original eau de toilette performance runs on the gentler side, typically six to eight hours with moderate sillage that closes in toward the skin well before the scent itself fades completely. Its softness is also its main limitation: on dry skin, in cold weather, or next to a stronger fragrance, it can read as barely there by the evening’s second half, and later concentrations of the same name were released partly to answer that exact complaint. Skip it if you want a fragrance that still announces itself six hours after you put it on.


## Gucci Guilty Pour Femme vs Armani Code: notes, longevity, and projection at a glance


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme Armani Code


Feel Layered, warm amber fougere floral Soft, linear tonka oriental spicy


Main notes Geranium, peach, lilac, amber Lemon, bergamot, olive blossom, tonka bean


Lasts About 7 to 9 hours, stronger early sillage About 6 to 8 hours, gentle, close sillage


Best for Evenings, fall, date night Subtle evening wear, cooler months


## Which is better, Gucci Guilty Pour Femme or Armani Code?


The differentiator is projection and pace, not occasion, since both are aimed at evenings. Gucci Guilty Pour Femme changes across three stages and pushes harder, especially in the first couple of hours. Armani Code arrives close to its final form almost immediately and stays soft and close for most of the wear. Someone who wants a fragrance felt across a room should lean toward Guilty Pour Femme; someone who wants a fragrance only noticed up close should lean toward Code. Reapplication habits differ too, since Code’s softer performance means a midday touch-up is more often necessary than it is with Guilty Pour Femme.


The short answer


Choose Gucci Guilty Pour Femme if you want a layered floral that projects with real presence for a few hours before settling. Choose Armani Code if you want a soft, consistent tonka-driven scent that stays close rather than filling a room.


Projection this different rarely shows up on a testing strip, so the difference is easiest to judge across an actual evening out.


Wear it through a full month before deciding on a bottle.

## Frequently asked questions


What does Gucci Guilty Pour Femme smell like?


It opens on pink pepper and peach, moves through a geranium and lilac heart, and finishes on amber, patchouli, and white musk with a trace of vanilla. That base is what actually lingers on skin and fabric.


What does Armani Code smell like?


Armani Code opens with lemon and bergamot, moves into olive blossom, and settles into tonka bean, leather, and soft woods. It reads soft, warm, and faintly sweet, with little dramatic change along the way.


What is the main difference between Gucci Guilty Pour Femme and Armani Code?


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme moves through three distinct stages and projects more strongly, especially early on. Armani Code stays close to one soft, tonka-driven impression from start to finish and projects more gently throughout.


Which projects more, Gucci Guilty Pour Femme or Armani Code?


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme projects harder, particularly in its first couple of hours. The original Armani Code eau de toilette is a comparatively soft performer that sits closer to the skin for most of its wear.


Is Armani Code a strong, long-lasting fragrance?


Not especially in its original eau de toilette form. Expect roughly six to eight hours with moderate sillage that fades toward a close skin scent, softer than many fragrances in the same oriental spicy category.


Which is better for a night out, Gucci Guilty Pour Femme or Armani Code?


Gucci Guilty Pour Femme is the more noticeable choice if you want the fragrance to carry into the later hours. Armani Code suits you better if you prefer something soft and close that a date has to lean in to notice.
